He further argued that the finding of the High Court Division as to genuineness of the kabuliyats are based on no evidence on record in as much as P.W.5, Abul Hossain, Tahshilder of the concerned Tahsil Office stated that kahitinans have been opened in the name of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs paid rents from 1379-1397 Bangla Shal and as such, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. 

 19. He also argued that the Government did not challenge the settlement cases and the kabuliyats thereunder and opened Khatians in the name of the plaintiffs and accepted rents from them as such the Government is stopped from challenging the right, title and possession of the plaintiffs. 

 20. Mr. Md. Ashraf Ali, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent Nos.1-12, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He adds that alleged Kabuliyat of the plaintiff has not been registered and no title has been accrued in fovour of the plaintiffs and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 23. It is admitted that suit land has been recorded in the name of Government as Khas land and classification of land has been shown as Khal (খাল) whereas the plaintiff claimed to have taken settlement of such land from the Government as Naal (খাল) land as it appears from their Kabuliyat and mutated Khatian. 

 25. The learned Judge of the Appellate Court without adverting to the aforesaid finding of the trial Court came to a conclusion that though the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in respect of suit land since the Government has not approved and registered their Kabuliyat but observed that the plaintiff-petitioners have been able to prove their possession and-as such, they are entitled to retain the same until they are evicted and as such may be granted permanent injection. 

 26. It appears to us that the classification of the suit land has been shown as Khal and the same has been re-excavated on formulating project which goes to show that the Kabuliyats of the plaintiffs are forged documents and not approved by the authority. 

 27. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners (plaintiffs) argued that the petitioners (plaintiffs) submitted their Kabuliyat before the Government body along with a prayer for approval and registration of the same and as such, they are entitled to retain possession. But we find that the classification of land has been shown as khal which has been re-excavated after formulating various development projects as it appears from the written statements and evidence of the defendants. 

 28. Furthermore, P.W.3 deposed that he could not say as to how much land are being possessed by the petitioners (plaintiffs) and P.W.4 corroborated P.W.3 to the effect that he could not say as to how much land was being possessed by the plaintiffs from which plot. Thus, it appears that the petitioners (plaintiff) failed to adduce corroborating evidence in support of their uninterrupted possession. Over and above signing and approval of the petitioner's Kabuliyat is absolute domain of the Government wherein the Court has nothing to do especially when the development project has been taken for re-excavation of the khal.
